key_insight: A D-gun Al2O3-TiO2 coating substantially improves the wear resistance of Ti-6Al-4V, and random forest best predicts wear from operating conditions.
engineering_relevance: The study links detonation-sprayed ceramic coatings with data-driven wear prediction, useful for aerospace, biomedical, and marine surface engineering.
method: Applied ~200 µm Al2O3-TiO2 coating to Ti-6Al-4V using a detonation gun process.
Evaluated tribological performance with ASTM G99 pin-on-disc tests over 40–100 N and 100–200 rpm.
Trained ANN, k-nearest neighbours, and random forest models to predict wear from sliding parameters.
evidence_signal: Experiments and microscopy showed reduced wear and protective tribo-layer formation on coated samples, while random forest had the lowest mean percentage error and mean squared error among the tested models.
watch_item: The machine-learning results are likely tied to the specific test window and coating/process settings, so broader generalization needs validation on more operating conditions and materials.
paper_title: Tribological enhancement of Al 2 O 3 -TiO 2 D-gun coated Ti-6Al-4V alloy: A machine learning approach
